chunks: From him, and a number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, altogether, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Ash'ari, from Ibn al-Qaddah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The Commander of the Faithful (blessings of God upon him) said: 'The crowing of the rooster is its prayer (salat), and the flapping of its wings are its bowing (ruku') and its prostration (sujud).'

key_terms.رُكُوعُهُ وَسُجُودُهُ: Its bowing and prostration — the wing-beating of the rooster is analogized to the ruku' and sujud of the human prayer
key_terms.صِيَاحُ الدِّيكِ: The crowing of the rooster — understood as a form of tasbih (glorification) and salat specific to this creature

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Ali say about the rooster's prayer in hadith?
ai.summary: Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (AS) quotes Imam Ali (AS) teaching that the rooster's natural behaviors — its crow and wing-beats — constitute acts of worship corresponding to the Islamic prayer postures of salat, ruku', and sujud. This cosmological teaching reflects the Shia Imami understanding that all creation engages in worship of God in ways unique to their nature, a concept rooted in Quranic verses affirming the universal glorification of God by all creatures. It underscores the spiritual significance of the rooster and explains the hadith tradition encouraging keeping roosters due to their worshipful nature.

en.hubeali:
From him, from a number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, altogether, from Ja’far Bin Muhammad Al Ashary, from Ibn Al Qaddah, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The shrieking of the rooster is its Prayer, and the flapping of its wings are its bowings and its prostrations’.
en.sarwar: 6. It is narrated from the narrator of the previous Hadith from A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad all from Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Ash‘ariy from ibn al-Qaddah who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that ’Amir al-Mu’minin has said, ‘Crowing of the rooster is its Salat (prayer) and flipping of its wings is its Ruku’ (bowing down on one’s knees) and Sujud (prostrations).”’
